But I'll sing about your strength. In the morning I'll sing out about your faithful love. You've been my high tower, my shelter when trouble hits. 🎶
My Strength, I'll sing my praise to you. God is my high tower, the God who shows me mercy.

For the music director, to “The Lily of the Covenant.” A teaching poem by David, when he fought Aram Naharaim and Aram Zobah, and Joab came back and killed twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. God, you've rejected us and broken us down. You've been angry. Bring us back.
You shook the land and tore it open. Mend the cracks, because it's still shaking.
You put your people through hard things. You made us drink wine that left us staggering.
You gave those who revere you a banner to raise for the truth. Selah.
Save us with your right hand and answer us, so the people you love can be rescued.
God spoke from his sanctuary: “I'll triumph. I'll divide up Shechem and measure out the valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, and so is Manasseh. Ephraim is the helmet that guards my head. Judah is my scepter.
Moab is my washbasin. I'll toss my sandal on Edom. I'll shout in victory over Philistia.”
Who's going to bring me into the fortified city? Who has led me to Edom?
God, haven't you rejected us? You don't march out with our armies anymore.
Help us against our enemy, because human help gets us nowhere.
With God we'll stand strong, because he's the one who will trample our enemies. 🙏
For the music director. For a stringed instrument. By David. God, hear my cry. Listen to my prayer.
From the ends of the earth, I'll call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that's higher than I am.
You've been my shelter, a strong tower where my enemy can't reach me.
I'll live in your tent forever. I'll take shelter under your wings. Selah.
God, you heard my vows. You gave me the inheritance of those who revere your name.
You'll give the king a long life. His years will stretch through generations.
He'll stay on his throne in God's presence forever. Let your faithful love and truth guard him.
I'll sing praise to your name forever and keep my vows day by day. 🎶
For the music director. To Jeduthun. A psalm by David. My soul finds rest in God alone. He's the one who saves me.
He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I won't be shaken badly.
How long will you keep coming at one person? Will you all knock him down like a leaning wall or a fence about to fall?
They're set on dragging him down from his high place. They love lies. They bless him out loud while cursing him inside. Selah.
My soul, wait quietly for God alone. My hope comes from him.
He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I won't be shaken.
My rescue and my honor come from God. He's my solid rock and my shelter.
Trust him all the time, everyone. Pour out your heart to him. God is our shelter. Selah.
People of low rank are a breath. People of high rank are an illusion. Put them all on the scale and they weigh less than a breath.
Don't count on squeezing people or pin your hopes on what you steal. If your money grows, don't let it have your heart.
God spoke once, and I've heard it twice: power belongs to God.
Faithful love belongs to you too, Lord, because you repay each person for what they've done.

A psalm by David, when he was in the desert of Judah. God, you're my God. I'm looking for you with everything I've got. My soul is thirsty for you. My whole body longs for you in this dry, worn-out land with no water.
I've seen you in the sanctuary and looked on your power and glory.
Your faithful love is better than life itself, so I'll praise you out loud.
I'll bless you as long as I live. I'll raise my hands in your name. 🙌
My soul will be as satisfied as if I'd eaten the richest food. With joy I'll sing your praise
when I remember you in bed and think about you through the watches of the night.
You've been my help. I'll celebrate in the shadow of your wings.
My soul clings to you. Your right hand holds me up.
Those who want to end my life will go down into the depths of the earth.
They'll fall to the sword and become food for jackals.
But the king will celebrate in God. Everyone who swears by God will glory in him, because the mouths of liars will be shut.
For the music director. A psalm by David. God, hear me as I bring you my troubles. Keep me safe from the enemy I fear.
Hide me from what the wicked are plotting and from the noisy crowd of people doing evil.
They sharpen their tongues like swords and aim their deadly words like arrows,
ready to fire from hiding at someone innocent. They shoot without warning and without fear.
They hype each other up to do wrong and talk about setting traps in secret. “Who's going to see them?” they say.
They scheme to do injustice and say, “We've got the perfect plan!” The human mind and heart can be so cunning.
But God will shoot at them. An arrow will strike them down without warning.
Their own words will be their undoing. Everyone who sees them will shake their heads.
Everyone will be afraid. They'll tell what God has done and take it to heart.
People who do what's right will rejoice in the LORD and run to him for shelter. Everyone with an upright heart will praise him! 🙌
For the music director. A psalm by David. A song. God, praise waits for you in Zion. There we'll keep the vows we made to you.
You hear prayer, and everyone will come to you.
My sins overwhelmed me, but you made atonement for our wrongs.
Blessed are those you choose and bring close to live in your courts. We'll have our fill of the goodness of your house, your holy temple.
God who saves us, you answer us with awesome deeds of righteousness. You're the hope of the farthest places on earth and of people far out at sea.
You formed the mountains by your power, clothed in strength.
You quiet the roar of the seas, the roar of their waves, and the uproar of the nations.
Even people far away stand in awe of your wonders. You make the dawn and the evening sing for joy.
You come to the earth and water it, making it rich. Your river is full of water. You give people grain, because that's how you planned it.
You soak the furrows and level the ridges. You soften the soil with rain and bless what grows.
You crown the year with your bounty. Your carts overflow with good things.
The wilderness grasslands overflow, and the hills are dressed in joy.
The pastures are covered in flocks, and the valleys are dressed in grain. They shout for joy and sing! 🌾
For the music director. A song. A psalm. Shout for joy to God, all the earth! 🙌
Sing about the glory of his name! Give him glory and praise!
Tell God, “What you've done is awesome! Your power is so great that your enemies give in before you.
The whole earth will worship you and sing to you. They'll sing praise to your name.” Selah.
Come see what God has done, the awe-inspiring things he's done for people.
He turned the sea into dry land. They crossed the river on foot. That's where we rejoiced in him.
He rules by his power forever and keeps his eyes on the nations. Let those who rebel never rise up against him. Selah.
Praise our God, all you peoples! Let everyone hear you praise him.
He keeps us alive and keeps our feet from slipping.
God, you put us to the test. You refined us the way silver gets refined.
You brought us into prison and put a heavy load on our backs.
You let people ride over our heads. We went through fire and water, and you brought us out to a place of abundance.
I'll come into your temple with burnt offerings. I'll keep the vows I made to you,
the promises I spoke out loud when I was in trouble.
I'll bring burnt offerings of fat animals and offer rams, bulls, and goats to you. Selah.
Come listen, all you who revere God. I'll tell you what he did for me.
I cried out to him, and I praised him out loud.
If I'd held on to sin in my heart, the Lord wouldn't have listened.
But God really did listen. He heard me when I prayed.
Bless God! He heard my prayer and kept showing me his faithful love.
For the music director. On strings. A psalm. A song. May God show us mercy, bless us, and make his face shine on us. Selah.
So your way will be known on earth and your salvation among all the nations.
May the peoples praise you, God. May every people praise you.
Let the nations celebrate and sing for joy! You judge the peoples fairly and guide the nations on earth. Selah.
May the peoples praise you, God. May every people praise you.
The earth has given its harvest. God, our own God, will bless us.
God will bless us, and people to the ends of the earth will stand in awe of him. 🙌
For the music director. A psalm by David. A song. Let God rise up! Let his enemies scatter! Let everyone who hates him run from him.
Drive them off like smoke in the wind. As wax melts in front of a fire, let the wicked perish in God's presence.
Let the righteous celebrate. Let them rejoice before God and be glad.
Sing to God! Sing praise to his name! Lift up the one who rides on the clouds. The LORD is his name! Celebrate before him!
God in his holy home is a father to the fatherless and a defender of widows.
God gives lonely people a family and leads prisoners out singing. Those who rebel live in a land scorched by the sun.
God, when you went ahead of your people, when you marched through the wilderness... Selah.
The earth shook and rain poured from the sky in the presence of the God of Sinai, in the presence of God, the God of Israel.
God, you sent plenty of rain and revived your inheritance when it was worn out.
Your people settled there. God, in your goodness you made a place for the poor.
The Lord gave the word. A huge crowd spread the news.
“The kings and their armies are running! They're running!” The woman waiting at home divides up the plunder,
while you lie among the campfires. A dove's wings are covered in silver, its feathers shining with gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings there, snow fell on Zalmon.
Bashan's mountains are majestic. Bashan's mountains are rugged.
Why are you rugged mountains looking with envy at the mountain God chose to rule from? The LORD will live there forever.
God's chariots number in the tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands. The Lord is among them, coming from Sinai into the sanctuary.
You went up to the heights and led captives away. You received gifts from people, even from those who rebelled, so the LORD God could live there.
Bless the Lord! He carries our burdens every day. He's the God who saves us. Selah.
Our God is a God of rescue. Escape from death belongs to GOD, the Lord.
God will strike the heads of his enemies, the hairy scalps of people who keep doing wrong.
The Lord said, “I'll bring them back from Bashan. I'll bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so you can crush them and dip your feet in their blood, and your dogs can have their share of your enemies.”
They've seen your procession, God, the procession of my God and King into the sanctuary.
The singers went first, the musicians came next, and the women played tambourines among them. 🎶
“Bless God in your gatherings! Bless the Lord in the assembly of Israel!”
There's little Benjamin leading them, the princes of Judah with their council, and the princes of Zebulun and Naphtali.
Your God has called up your strength. God, make strong what you've done for us.
Kings will bring you gifts because of your temple in Jerusalem.
Rebuke the wild beast in the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples. Trample the bars of silver. Scatter the nations that love war.
Princes will come from Egypt. Ethiopia will hurry to stretch out her hands to God.
Sing to God, kingdoms of the earth! Sing praise to the Lord. Selah.
He rides across the highest heavens, there from ancient times. Listen! He raises his voice, a mighty voice.
Give God credit for his strength! His majesty is over Israel, and his strength reaches the skies.
You're awesome in your sanctuaries, God. The God of Israel gives his people strength and power. Praise God!
For the music director, to “Lilies.” By David. Save me, God! The water's up to my neck!
I'm sinking in deep mud with nowhere to plant my feet. I've gone into deep water, and the flood is sweeping over me.
I'm worn out from crying. My throat is dry. My eyes are giving out from looking for my God.
The people who hate me for no reason outnumber the hairs on my head. Powerful people are out to end me, though they have no cause against me. I'm made to pay back what I never took.
God, you know how foolish I've been. I can't hide my sins from you.
Lord GOD of Armies, don't let people who wait for you be shamed because of me. God of Israel, don't let those who seek you be disgraced because of me.
I've taken insults for your sake. Shame covers my face.
I'm a stranger to my brothers, an outsider to my own mother's children.
My passion for your house consumes me. The insults people throw at you have landed on me.
When I cried and went without food, they used it against me.
When I put on sackcloth, I became their punch line.
The people who sit at the gate talk about me. Drunks make up songs about me.
But I pray to you, LORD, at a time when you'll welcome my prayer. God, in your abundant faithful love, answer me with the sure rescue you give.
Pull me out of the mud. Don't let me sink. Rescue me from those who hate me and from the deep water.
Don't let the flood sweep over me, the depths swallow me, or the pit close its mouth on me.
Answer me, LORD, because your faithful love is good. Turn toward me in your deep compassion.
Don't hide your face from your servant. I'm in trouble. Answer me quick!
Come close and redeem my life. Ransom me from my enemies.
You know the insults, shame, and disgrace I've taken. You see every one of my enemies.
Their insults broke my heart, and the weight is crushing me. I looked for someone to have pity, and nobody did. I looked for comfort, and found none.
They put poison in my food and gave me vinegar when I was thirsty.
Let their own table become a snare. Let it be their payback and their trap.
Darken their eyes so they can't see, and let their backs stay bent.
Pour out your outrage on them. Let your fierce anger catch up with them.
Let their home go empty. Let nobody live in their tents.
They go after the one you wounded and talk about the pain of those you've hurt.
Charge them with one crime after another. Don't let them share in your righteousness.
Erase them from the book of life. Don't list them with the people who do right.
I'm hurting and in distress. God, let your salvation keep me safe.
I'll praise God's name with a song and tell how great he is by giving thanks. 🎶
That will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.
The humble have seen it and are glad. All you who seek God, let your hearts come alive.
The LORD listens to people in need and doesn't look down on his people in captivity.
Let heaven and earth praise him, along with the seas and everything moving in them!
God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah. His people will settle there and own the land.
The children of his servants will inherit it. Those who love his name will live there.
For the music director. By David. A reminder. God, hurry and rescue me. LORD, come help me quick.
Let the people trying to take my life end up ashamed and confused. Turn back those who want to see me ruined, and let them go away in disgrace.
Let the people who taunt me with “Aha! Aha!” turn back in shame.
Let everyone who seeks you celebrate and be glad in you. Let those who love the way you save keep saying, “Lift up God!” 🙌
I'm poor and in need. God, come to me quick. You're my help and my rescuer. LORD, don't wait.
LORD, I run to you for shelter. Don't ever let me be put to shame.
Rescue me in your righteousness and get me out of danger. Lean in, hear me, and save me.
Be the rock I can always run to. Give the word to save me, because you're my rock and my fortress.
My God, rescue me from the grip of the wicked, from people who are unjust and cruel.
Lord GOD, you're my hope. I've trusted you since I was young.
I've leaned on you since I was in the womb. You brought me out of my mother's womb. I'll always praise you.
Many people look at me in wonder, and you're my strong shelter.
My mouth will be full of praise for you and speak of your honor all day long.
Don't turn me away in my old age. Don't leave me when my strength gives out.
My enemies are talking about me. The people waiting to take my life are plotting together.
“God has left him,” they say. “Go after him and grab him. Nobody's coming to save him.”
God, don't stay far from me. My God, come help me quick.
Let my accusers be ashamed and swept away. Cover the people who want to hurt me with disgrace and scorn.
I'll keep hoping and give you even more praise.
All day I'll tell people about your righteousness and how you save, though I can't begin to count it all.
I'll come telling of the mighty things the Lord GOD has done. I'll speak of your righteousness, yours alone.
God, you've taught me since I was young. I'm still telling people about the amazing things you've done.
Even when I'm old and gray, God, don't leave me until I tell the next generation about your strength and everyone yet to come about your power.
God, your righteousness reaches to the heavens. You've done great things. God, who's like you?
You've let us see plenty of bitter trouble. You'll give me life again and bring us back up from the depths of the earth.
Give me greater honor and comfort me again.
My God, I'll praise your faithfulness on the harp. I'll sing to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel. 🎶
My lips will shout for joy! You've redeemed my soul, and I'll sing your praise!
I'll talk about your righteousness all day long, because the people who want to hurt me have been put to shame and left confused.
By Solomon. God, give the king your justice and give the royal son your righteousness.
He'll judge your people with righteousness and give the poor a fair hearing.
May the mountains bring prosperity to the people and the hills bring the fruit of righteousness.
He'll make sure the poor get justice, rescue the children of the needy, and break their oppressor's power.
People will revere you for as long as the sun and moon endure, through every generation.
He'll come down like rain on freshly cut grass, like showers watering the earth.
In his days, people who do right will flourish, and peace will overflow until the moon is gone.
He'll rule from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.
People in the wilderness will bow before him. His enemies will lick the dust.
The kings of Tarshish and the islands will bring tribute. The kings of Sheba and Seba will bring gifts.
All kings will bow before him. All nations will serve him.
He'll rescue people in need when they cry out, including the poor who have nobody to help them.
He'll show compassion to the poor and needy and save their lives.
He'll rescue them from oppression and violence. Their blood is precious to him.
May he live! May he receive gold from Sheba. People will pray for him continually and bless him all day long.
May grain grow in abundance across the land, swaying like the trees of Lebanon. Let it flourish like grass in the fields. 🌾
May his name last forever, for as long as the sun. People will be blessed through him. All nations will call him blessed.
Praise the LORD God, the God of Israel. He alone does amazing things.
Bless his glorious name forever! Let his glory fill the whole earth! Amen and amen. 🙌
This ends the prayers of David son of Jesse.
A psalm by Asaph. God really is good to Israel, to people whose hearts are pure.
But I almost lost my footing. My feet nearly slipped.
I envied the arrogant when I saw how well the wicked were doing.
They die without a struggle, and their strength holds up.
They don't carry the burdens other people do. They don't get hit with the same troubles.
So they wear pride like a chain around their necks and wrap themselves in violence.
Their eyes bulge with fat. Their conceit knows no limits.
They mock people and speak with malice. They act above everyone and threaten to crush them.
They mouth off against heaven, and their words run all over the earth.
So their people turn back to them and drink deeply of their abundance.
They say, “How would God know? Does the Most High know anything about this?”
Look at the wicked. They're always chilling, and their wealth keeps growing.
Did I keep my heart clean for nothing? Did I wash my hands in innocence for no reason?
I've been hurt all day and punished every morning.
If I'd said, “I'm going to talk like that,” I would've betrayed this generation of your children.
I tried to make sense of it, but it was too painful for me
until I went into God's sanctuary and thought about where they were headed.
You put them on slippery ground. You send them crashing into ruin.
How suddenly they're ruined! Terror sweeps them away completely.
Lord, they're like a dream that fades when someone wakes. When you rise, you'll treat their fantasies with contempt.
My soul was hurting. Bitterness got deep into my heart.
I was clueless and senseless, like a wild animal in front of you.
Still, I'm always with you. You've held my right hand.
You'll guide me with your counsel, then welcome me into glory.
Who do I have in heaven? There's nobody on earth I want besides you.
My body and heart can give out, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever. 🙏
Look, those who stay far from you will perish. You've destroyed everyone who has been unfaithful to you.
As for me, being close to God is good. I've made the Lord GOD my shelter so I can tell people everything you've done.
A psalm for reflection by Asaph. God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep in your pasture?
Remember the people you bought long ago, the tribe you redeemed as your inheritance. Remember Mount Zion, where you lived.
Walk through these ruins that never seem to end. Look at all the damage the enemy did in your sanctuary.
Your enemies roared right in the middle of your gathering. They planted their own banners there as signs.
They swung their axes like people chopping through a thicket.
Now they're smashing every carving with hatchets and hammers.
They burned your sanctuary to the ground. They defiled the place where your Name lived.
They thought, “We'll crush them completely.” They burned every place in the land where people worshiped God.
We see no signs. No prophet is left, and nobody among us knows how long this will last.
God, how long will the enemy mock you? Will they disrespect your name forever?
Why are you holding back your right hand? Take it from your chest and put an end to them!
Yet God has been my King from long ago, bringing rescue all across the earth.
You split the sea with your strength. You shattered the heads of the monsters in the water.
You crushed Leviathan's heads and gave him as food to people and desert creatures.
You opened up springs and streams. You dried up mighty rivers.
The day is yours, and so is the night. You set the light and the sun in place.
You set every boundary of the earth. You made summer and winter.
Remember how the enemy mocked you, LORD. Foolish people dragged your name through the dirt.
Don't hand your dove over to wild beasts. Don't forget the lives of your poor forever.
Honor your covenant. Violence has made a home in the dark places of the earth.
Don't send the oppressed away in shame. Let the poor and needy praise your name.
Get up, God! Take up your own case. Remember how fools mock you all day.
Don't forget what your enemies are shouting. The noise of those who rise against you keeps going up.
For the music director, to “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm by Asaph. A song. We thank you, God. We thank you because your Name is near. People tell of the amazing things you've done.
When I choose the appointed time, I'll judge fairly.
The earth and everyone on it may shake, but I hold its pillars steady. Selah.
I told the arrogant, “Quit flexing!” I told the wicked, “Don't raise your horn.
Don't hold your horn up high. Don't talk with your neck stiff in defiance.”
Being lifted up doesn't come from the east, the west, or the south.
God is the judge. He brings one person down and lifts another up.
The LORD holds a cup of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out, and the wicked of the earth drink every last drop.
I'll keep telling this forever. I'll sing praise to the God of Jacob. 🎶
I'll cut off all the horns of the wicked, and the horns of the righteous will be lifted high.
For the music director. On strings. A psalm by Asaph. A song. People in Judah know God. His name is great in Israel.
His tent is in Salem. His home is in Zion.
There he broke the flaming arrows, the shield, the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah.
You shine with glory, more majestic than mountains full of prey.
The bravest warriors lie stripped of their gear. They've slept their last sleep. None of them can lift a hand.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse fall into a dead sleep.
You're the one to be feared. Who can stand before you when you're angry?
You announced your judgment from heaven. The earth went silent in fear
when God rose to judge and save all the suffering people of the earth. Selah.
Even human anger ends up praising you. You hold back those who survive your wrath.
Make vows to the LORD your God and keep them! Let everyone around him bring gifts to the one they should stand in awe of.
He breaks the spirit of rulers. The kings of the earth fear him.
For the music director. To Jeduthun. A psalm by Asaph. I cry out to God! I'm calling on God for help, asking him to hear me.
When trouble hit, I sought the Lord. I kept my hand stretched out all night. My soul refused to be comforted.
I remember God and groan. I pour out my complaint, and my spirit feels overwhelmed. Selah.
You keep my eyes wide open. I'm too upset to speak.
I think back to the old days, to years long past.
I remember the song I used to sing at night. I search my heart and ask myself:
“Will the Lord reject us forever? Will he never show us favor again?
Is his faithful love gone for good? Has his promise failed for every generation?
Has God forgotten how to show grace? Has his anger made him hold back his compassion?” Selah.
Then I thought, “I'll hold on to this: the years when the Most High showed the strength of his right hand.”
I'll remember what the LORD has done. I'll remember the wonders you did long ago.
I'll think deeply about your work and take to heart what you've done.
God, your way is in the sanctuary. What god is as great as you?
You're the God who does wonders. You've shown your strength among the peoples.
You rescued your people with your own arm, the children of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw you, God. They saw you and twisted in fear. Even the depths shook.
The clouds poured out rain. Thunder echoed through the skies, and your arrows flashed all around.
Your thunder roared in the whirlwind. Lightning lit up the whole world. The earth trembled and shook. ⚡
Your path ran through the sea, right through the mighty waters, and nobody could see your footprints.
You led your people like a flock through the hands of Moses and Aaron.
A psalm for reflection by Asaph. My people, hear what I'm teaching. Listen closely to my words.
I'll speak in a parable and bring out hard truths from long ago,
things we've heard and known because our ancestors told us.
We won't hide them from their children. We'll tell the next generation why the LORD deserves praise, how strong he is, and what amazing things he's done.
He established a covenant in Jacob and gave Israel a teaching. He commanded our ancestors to pass it on to their children,
so the next generation would know, even children yet to be born. They'd grow up and tell their own children,
so they'd put their hope in God, remember what he's done, and keep his commands.
That way they wouldn't be like their ancestors, a stubborn generation that rebelled, whose hearts weren't loyal and whose spirits wouldn't stay faithful to God.
Ephraim's people were armed with bows, but on battle day they turned back.
They broke God's covenant and refused to live by his law.
They forgot what he'd done, all the wonders he'd shown them.
He did amazing things in front of their ancestors in Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.
He split the sea and let them cross. He piled the waters up like a wall.
By day he led them with a cloud, and all night with the light of fire.
He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them water to drink as freely as from the depths.
He brought streams out of the rock and made water flow down like rivers.
Still, they kept sinning against him and rebelling against the Most High in the desert.
In their hearts they put God to the test by demanding the food they craved.
They spoke against God: “Can God set a table in the wilderness?
Sure, he struck the rock and water gushed out until streams overflowed. But can he give us bread? Can he get meat for his people?”
The LORD heard and was angry. Fire flared against Jacob, and anger rose against Israel,
because they didn't believe God or trust him to save them.
Even so, he commanded the skies above and opened heaven's doors.
He rained down manna for them to eat and gave them food from the sky.
People ate the bread of angels. He sent them enough food to eat their fill.
He sent the east wind blowing through the skies. By his power he directed the south wind.
He rained meat down on them like dust, birds as countless as sand by the sea.
He dropped them right in the camp, all around where they lived.
They ate until they were full. He gave them exactly what they craved.
But they wouldn't let go of their cravings. The food was still in their mouths
when God's anger rose against them. He killed some of their strongest and struck down Israel's young men.
Even after all that, they kept sinning and wouldn't believe in his wonders.
So he brought their days to nothing and filled their years with terror.
When he struck them down, they came looking for him. They turned back and searched for God with real urgency.
They remembered that God was their rock, that the Most High God was their redeemer.
But they flattered him with their mouths and lied to him with their tongues.
Their hearts weren't right with him, and they weren't faithful to his covenant.
Yet he showed mercy. He forgave their wrongdoing and held back from destroying them. Again and again he turned his anger away and held back the full force of his wrath.
He remembered they were only flesh, like a wind that blows past and never comes back.
How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and hurt him in the desert!
They put God to the test again and pushed the Holy One of Israel to anger.
They forgot his power and the day he rescued them from their enemy.
They forgot how he showed his signs in Egypt and his wonders in the fields of Zoan.
He turned their rivers and streams into blood so they couldn't drink.
He sent swarms of flies that devoured them and frogs that brought destruction.
He handed their crops over to caterpillars and the fruit of their work to locusts.
He destroyed their vines with hail and their sycamore figs with frost.
He left their livestock to the hail and their flocks to blazing lightning.
He unleashed fierce anger on them, wrath, outrage, and trouble, with a band of angels bringing disaster.
He cleared a path for his anger. He didn't spare them from death but left their lives to the plague.
He struck every firstborn in Egypt, the first of their strength in the tents of Ham.
But he led his own people out like sheep and guided them through the wilderness like a flock.
He led them safely so they had no reason to fear. The sea swept over their enemies.
He brought them to the edge of his holy land, to this mountain his right hand had taken.
He drove out nations ahead of them, measured out land for their inheritance, and settled Israel's tribes in their tents.
Yet they tested and rebelled against God Most High and refused to keep his instructions.
They turned away and acted just as faithlessly as their ancestors. They twisted like a bow you can't trust.
They made him angry with their places of worship on the heights and stirred his jealousy with their carved images.
When God heard, he was angry and recoiled from Israel.
He left the tent at Shiloh, the tent he'd set up among people.
He let his strength go into captivity and gave his glory into his enemy's hands.
He handed his people over to the sword and was angry with his own inheritance.
Fire devoured their young men, and their young women never heard a wedding song.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows couldn't even weep.
Then the Lord woke as if from sleep, like a warrior shouting from the force of wine.
He struck his enemies and drove them back, leaving them in lasting disgrace.
He rejected Joseph's tent and passed over the tribe of Ephraim.
He chose the tribe of Judah and Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth he set in place forever.
He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds.
He brought David away from tending mother sheep and their young to shepherd Jacob, his people, and Israel, his inheritance.
David shepherded them with an honest heart and guided them with skilled hands.
A psalm by Asaph. God, nations have invaded your inheritance. They've defiled your holy temple and left Jerusalem in piles of rubble.
They left your servants' bodies for the birds of the sky and the bodies of your faithful people for wild animals to eat.
They spilled their blood like water all around Jerusalem. Nobody was there to bury them.
We're a disgrace to our neighbors. People all around us scoff and laugh at us.
How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out your wrath on nations that don't know you and kingdoms that don't call on your name,
because they've devoured Jacob and wrecked his homeland.
Don't hold our ancestors' wrongs against us. Let your tender mercy meet us quickly. We're desperate.
God who saves us, help us for the glory of your name. Rescue us and forgive our sins for the sake of your name. 🙏
Why should the nations ask, “Where's their God?” Let the nations see, right in front of us, that you're avenging the blood of your servants.
Let the prisoners' sighs reach you. By your great power, keep alive the people sentenced to die.
Lord, pay our neighbors back seven times over for the insults they threw at you.
Then we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, will thank you forever. We'll tell of your praise from generation to generation.
For the music director, to “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A psalm by Asaph. Listen, Shepherd of Israel. You lead Joseph like a flock. You sit above the cherubim. Shine out!
In front of Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your strength! Come save us!
Bring us back, God. Let your face shine on us, and we'll be saved.
LORD God of Armies, how long will you be angry when your people pray?
You fed them bread made of tears and gave them tears to drink by the bowlful.
You made us the cause of fights among our neighbors, and our enemies laugh about us.
Bring us back, God of Armies. Let your face shine on us, and we'll be saved.
You brought a vine out of Egypt, drove out nations, and planted it. 🌿
You cleared the ground for it. Its roots went deep, and it filled the land.
Its shadow covered mountains, and its branches were like God's cedars.
Its branches reached the sea, and its shoots stretched to the River.
Why did you break down its walls and let everyone passing by pick from it?
A wild boar from the woods tears it up, and animals from the fields feed on it.
God of Armies, please turn back. Look down from heaven, see what's happening, and come tend this vine,
the root your right hand planted, the branch you made strong for yourself.
It's been burned and cut down. They perish when you rebuke them.
Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand, the son of man you made strong for yourself.
Then we won't turn away from you. Bring us back to life, and we'll call on your name.
Bring us back, LORD God of Armies. Let your face shine on us, and we'll be saved.
For the music director. On an instrument of Gath. By Asaph. Sing out to God, our strength! Give a joyful shout to the God of Jacob!
Start the song. Bring the tambourine, the sweet-sounding lyre, and the harp. 🎶
Blow the trumpet at the new moon, at the full moon, on our feast day.
This is a rule for Israel, an ordinance from the God of Jacob.
He set it in place as a covenant for Joseph when he went out over Egypt. I heard a language I didn't know.
“I lifted the load off his shoulder. I freed his hands from the basket.
You called when you were in trouble, and I rescued you. I answered from where the thunder was hidden. I tested you at the waters of Meribah.” Selah.
“Listen, my people, while I testify to you. Israel, if only you'd hear me!
Don't let any strange god among you. Don't worship a foreign god.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I'll fill it.
But my people wouldn't listen to me. Israel wanted nothing to do with me.
So I let them follow their stubborn hearts and go with their own plans.
If only my people would listen to me! If only Israel would walk in my ways!
I'd soon bring their enemies down and turn my hand against the people who oppose them.
Those who hate the LORD would cringe before him, and their punishment would last forever.
But he would feed his people with the finest wheat. I'd give you your fill of honey from the rock.”
A psalm by Asaph. God presides over the great assembly. He judges among the gods.
“How long will you judge unfairly and play favorites with the wicked?” Selah.
“Stand up for the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Protect the rights of poor and oppressed people.
Rescue the weak and needy. Get them out of the grip of the wicked.”
They have no clue and no understanding. They wander around in darkness. All the foundations of the earth shake.
I said, “You are gods. All of you are children of the Most High.
Even so, you'll die like mortals and fall like any other ruler.”
Rise up, God, and judge the earth, because all the nations are your inheritance.
A song. A psalm by Asaph. God, don't stay silent. Don't stay quiet or sit still.
Look, your enemies are getting loud. Those who hate you are lifting their heads.
They're scheming against your people, plotting against the ones you cherish.
“Come on,” they say, “let's wipe them out as a nation so nobody remembers Israel's name.”
They're all in on the same plan. They've joined forces against you.
The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites are in it, along with Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, plus Philistia and the people of Tyre.
Assyria has joined them too, backing up Lot's descendants. Selah.
Do to them what you did to Midian, to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River.
They died at Endor and became like dung on the ground.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, “Let's take God's pasturelands for ourselves.”
My God, make them like tumbleweed, like chaff scattered by the wind.
Like fire that burns through a forest or flames that set mountains ablaze,
chase them with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.
Let confusion cover their faces so they'll seek your name, LORD.
Let them be ashamed and terrified forever. Let them be disgraced and perish,
so they know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over the whole earth.
For the music director. On an instrument of Gath. A psalm by the sons of Korah. LORD of Armies, your home is so beautiful!
My soul aches for the LORD's courts. My heart and my whole body cry out for the living God.
Even the sparrow finds a home and the swallow finds a nest for her young near your altars, LORD of Armies, my King and my God.
Blessed are those who live in your house. They're always praising you. Selah.
Blessed are those who draw their strength from you and have their hearts set on the journey to your house.
When they pass through the Valley of Weeping, they turn it into a place of springs. The autumn rain covers it with blessings.
They grow stronger as they go. Every one of them appears before God in Zion.
LORD God of Armies, hear my prayer. Listen, God of Jacob. Selah.
God, our shield, look on the face of your anointed one.
One day in your courts beats a thousand. I'd sooner stand at the door of my God's house than live in the tents of wickedness.
The LORD God is a sun and a shield. He gives grace and glory. He holds back no good thing from those who live with integrity. ☀️
LORD of Armies, blessed is anyone who trusts in you.
For the music director. A psalm by the sons of Korah. LORD, you showed favor to your land. You restored Jacob's fortunes.
You forgave your people's wrongdoing and covered all their sin. Selah.
You set aside all your wrath and turned away from your fierce anger.
Bring us back, God who saves us. Let your anger against us come to an end.
Will you stay angry with us forever? Will your anger go on through every generation?
Won't you bring us back to life so your people can find joy in you again?
Show us your faithful love, LORD. Give us your salvation.
I'll listen to what God, the LORD, says. He'll speak peace to his people, those faithful to him. Let them stay away from their old foolish ways.
His salvation is close to those who revere him, so glory can live in our land.
Mercy and truth meet up. Righteousness and peace greet each other with a kiss.
Truth springs up from the ground, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
The LORD will give what's good, and our land will bring in a harvest. 🌾
Righteousness goes out ahead of him, getting the path ready for his steps.
A prayer by David. LORD, hear me and answer me. I'm poor and in need.
Guard my life, because I'm faithful to you. My God, save your servant who trusts you.
Show me mercy, Lord. I'm calling on you all day long.
Bring joy to your servant's soul. Lord, I lift my soul to you.
Lord, you're good and ready to forgive. You have more than enough faithful love for everyone who calls on you.
LORD, hear my prayer. Listen to me pleading for help.
When trouble hits, I'll call on you, because you'll answer me.
No one among the gods is like you, Lord. Nobody does what you do.
Every nation you've made will come and worship before you, Lord. They'll give your name glory.
You're great and do amazing things. You alone are God.
Teach me your way, LORD, and I'll walk in your truth. Give me an undivided heart that reveres your name.
Lord my God, I'll praise you with my whole heart. I'll give your name glory forever. 🙏
Your faithful love for me is great. You rescued my life from the deepest part of Sheol.
God, proud people have risen against me. A gang of violent people is out to take my life. They don't give you a thought.
But you, Lord, are merciful and gracious, slow to anger and overflowing with faithful love and truth.
Turn toward me and show me mercy! Give your servant your strength. Save the son of your servant.
Show me a sign of your goodness so those who hate me will see it and be ashamed. LORD, you've helped me and given me comfort.
A psalm by the sons of Korah. A song. God laid his foundation in the holy mountains.
The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the homes of Jacob.
People say glorious things about you, city of God. Selah.
I'll list Rahab and Babylon among those who know me. Look at Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia too. “This one was born there.”
People will say about Zion, “This one and that one were born here.” The Most High himself will keep her standing.
When the LORD records the peoples, he'll count them and say, “This one was born there.” Selah.
Singers and dancers alike say, “All my springs are in you.” 🎶

A song. A psalm by the sons of Korah. For the music director, to “The Suffering of Affliction.” A psalm for reflection by Heman the Ezrahite. LORD, God who saves me, I've cried out to you day and night.
Let my prayer reach you. Lean in and hear my cry.
My soul is full of trouble, and my life is getting close to Sheol.
People already count me among those going down to the pit. I'm like someone with nobody to help,
left among the dead like those killed and laid in the grave, the ones you remember no more. They're cut off from your hand.
You've put me in the deepest pit, down in the darkest depths.
Your wrath is heavy on me. Every wave you've sent has crashed over me. Selah.
You've taken my friends away and made them recoil from me. I'm trapped with no way out.
Grief has dimmed my eyes. LORD, I call to you every day and stretch out my hands to you.
Do you show your wonders to the dead? Do the departed rise and praise you? Selah.
Does anyone speak of your faithful love in the grave, or your faithfulness in Destruction?
Do people know your wonders in the dark, or your righteousness in the land where everything is forgotten?
But I cry out to you, LORD. My prayer comes to you first thing in the morning.
LORD, why do you reject me? Why do you hide your face from me?
I've suffered and been close to death since I was young. Your terrors leave me overwhelmed.
Your fierce wrath has swept over me. Your terrors have cut me off.
They surround me like water all day long. They've swallowed me up completely.
You've put the people I love and my friends far from me. My friends are lost in darkness.
A psalm for reflection by Ethan the Ezrahite. I'll sing about the LORD's faithful love forever. I'll tell every generation how faithful you are.
This is what I say: “Your love stands firm forever. You set the heavens in place, and your faithfulness stands there.”
“I made a covenant with my chosen one. I swore to David my servant,
‘I'll establish your descendants forever and build up your throne through every generation.’” Selah.
The heavens will praise your wonders, LORD, and the assembly of the holy ones will praise your faithfulness.
Who in the skies compares to the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD?
God inspires awe in the council of the holy ones. Everyone around him reveres him above all.
LORD God of Armies, who is mighty like you? LORD, your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule the raging sea. When its waves rise, you calm them.
You shattered Rahab like someone struck down. You scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.
The heavens are yours. So is the earth, the world and everything in it. You laid their foundations.
You made the north and the south. Tabor and Hermon celebrate your name.
Your arm is mighty. Your hand is strong, and your right hand is raised high.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne. Faithful love and truth go on ahead of you.
Blessed are the people who learn to shout your praise. LORD, they walk in the light of your presence.
They celebrate your name all day. Your righteousness lifts them up.
You're the glory of their strength. Your favor raises up our horn.
Our shield belongs to the LORD, and our king belongs to the Holy One of Israel.
Then you spoke to your faithful ones in a vision: “I gave strength to a warrior. I lifted up a young man from among the people.
I found David my servant and anointed him with my holy oil.
My hand will hold him steady, and my arm will give him strength.
No enemy will exact tribute from him. No wicked person will oppress him.
I'll bring down his enemies in front of him and strike those who hate him.
My faithfulness and faithful love will stay with him. In my name his horn will be lifted high.
I'll set his hand over the sea and his right hand over the rivers.
He'll call out to me, ‘You're my Father, my God, and the rock who saves me!’
I'll make him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
I'll keep showing him faithful love forever. My covenant with him will stand firm.
I'll make his descendants last forever and his throne endure as long as the heavens.
If his children abandon my law and stop living by my rulings,
if they break my statutes and ignore my commands,
I'll punish their sin with the rod and their wrongdoing with blows.
But I won't take my faithful love away from him entirely or let my faithfulness fail.
I won't break my covenant or change a word I've spoken.
I've sworn by my holiness once for all. I won't lie to David.
His descendants will last forever, and his throne will endure before me like the sun.
It'll stand forever like the moon, a faithful witness in the sky.” Selah.
But you've rejected your anointed and turned him away in anger.
You've renounced your servant's covenant and dragged his crown through the dust.
You've torn down every fence around him and left his fortresses in ruins.
Everyone passing by robs him. His neighbors see him as a disgrace.
You've raised the right hand of his enemies and made everyone against him celebrate.
You turned back the edge of his sword and left him without support in battle.
You put an end to his splendor and threw his throne to the ground.
You cut his youth short and covered him with shame. Selah.
How long, LORD? Will you hide forever? Will your wrath burn like fire?
Remember how short my life is. How fleeting you've made the lives of us all!
Who can live without seeing death? Who can save their own life from the grip of Sheol? Selah.
Lord, where are the acts of faithful love you showed before, the ones you swore to David in your faithfulness?
Lord, remember the insults your servants bear. I carry the taunts of all those powerful peoples in my heart.
Your enemies are mocking, LORD. They mock your anointed one at every step.
Bless the LORD forever! Amen and amen. 🙌
A prayer by Moses, the man of God. Lord, you've been our home through every generation.
Before the mountains were born, before you shaped the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting, you are God.
You turn people back to dust and say, “Return, you mortals.”
A thousand years to you are like yesterday once it's gone, like one watch in the night.
You sweep people away as they sleep. In the morning they shoot up like fresh grass.
It sprouts and grows in the morning. By evening it's dried up and withered.
Your anger consumes us. Your wrath leaves us shaken.
You've set our wrongs in front of you. Even our secret sins are in the light of your presence.
All our days pass under your wrath. Our years end with a sigh.
We get seventy years, or eighty if we're strong. Even the best of them bring hard work and grief. They pass in a flash, and we fly away.
Who knows how powerful your anger is? Who reckons with your wrath and gives you the reverence you're due?
Teach us to count our days so we can grow wise at heart.
Relent, LORD! How long will it be? Show compassion to your servants!
Fill us with your faithful love in the morning so we can rejoice and be glad all our days. 🌅
Give us as many days of joy as the days you made us suffer, as many years as we've known trouble.
Let your servants see what you do and their children see your glory.
May the favor of the Lord our God rest on us. Make the work of our hands last. Yes, make the work of our hands last.
Anyone who makes their home in the shelter of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
I'll say of the LORD, “He's my shelter and my fortress, my God, the one I trust.”
He'll rescue you from the bird catcher's trap and from deadly disease.
He'll cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you'll find shelter. His faithfulness is your shield and your defense.
You won't fear the terror that comes at night or the arrow that flies by day,
the disease that moves in the dark or the destruction that strikes at noon.
A thousand may fall beside you and ten thousand at your right hand, but it won't come near you.
You'll look with your own eyes and see the wicked get what they've earned.
Because you've made the LORD your shelter and the Most High your home,
no harm will come to you, and no plague will come near where you live.
He'll command his angels to guard you wherever you go.
They'll lift you in their hands so you won't strike your foot against a stone.
You'll step on the lion and the cobra. You'll trample the young lion and the serpent underfoot.
“Because he loves me, I'll rescue him. I'll lift him out of reach because he knows my name.
He'll call on me, and I'll answer. I'll be with him when trouble hits. I'll rescue him and give him honor.
I'll satisfy him with a long life and show him my salvation.” 🙏
A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. It's good to thank the LORD and sing praise to your name, Most High,
to tell of your faithful love in the morning and your faithfulness every night,
with the ten-string lute, the harp, and the melody of the lyre. 🎶
LORD, what you've done has made me glad. I'll shout for joy at the work of your hands.
Your works are amazing, LORD! Your thoughts go so deep.
People without sense don't see it. Fools don't get this:
the wicked can spring up like grass and everyone doing evil can thrive, but they'll be destroyed forever.
You, LORD, are on high forever.
Look, LORD, your enemies will perish. Everyone doing evil will be scattered.
You've raised my horn high like a wild ox's. I've been anointed with fresh oil.
My eyes have seen my enemies, and my ears have heard about the wicked who rise against me.
People who do what's right will flourish like palm trees and grow like cedars in Lebanon.
They're planted in the LORD's house. They'll thrive in our God's courts.
They'll still bear fruit in old age, full of sap and still green,
showing that the LORD is upright. He's my rock, and there is no wrongdoing in him.
The LORD reigns! He's dressed in majesty and armed with strength. The world stands firm. Nothing can shake it.
Your throne has stood since long ago. You are from everlasting.
The floods have risen, LORD. They've raised their voices. The floods lift up their waves.
Above the roar of mighty waters, above the breakers of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty. 🌊
Your statutes stand firm. Holiness adorns your house, LORD, forever.
LORD, God to whom vengeance belongs, shine out! God to whom vengeance belongs, shine out!
Rise up, Judge of the earth. Give the proud what they deserve.
LORD, how long will the wicked keep winning? How long?
Arrogant words pour out of them. Everyone doing evil is bragging.
LORD, they crush your people and hurt those who belong to you.
They kill widows and foreigners and murder children who have no father.
They say, “The LORD won't see. Jacob's God won't pay attention.”
Think about it, you people with no sense. You fools, when will you wise up?
The one who made the ear can hear, can't he? The one who formed the eye can see, can't he?
Won't the one who disciplines nations hold people to account? The one who teaches humanity knows.
The LORD knows people's thoughts. He knows how futile they are.
Blessed is anyone you discipline, LORD, anyone you teach from your law.
You give them rest through days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
The LORD won't reject his people or walk away from his inheritance.
Judgment will line up with what is right again, and everyone with an upright heart will follow it.
Who'll stand up for me against the wicked? Who'll take my side against people doing evil?
If the LORD hadn't helped me, I'd soon have gone down into silence.
When I said, “My foot is slipping!” your faithful love held me up, LORD.
When my mind is crowded with thoughts, your comfort brings joy to my soul. 🙏
Can a corrupt throne be on your side when it uses laws to bring about harm?
They join forces against people who do right and condemn innocent people to death.
But the LORD has been my high tower. My God is the rock where I take shelter.
He has brought their wrongdoing back on them. He'll cut them off in their own wickedness. The LORD our God will cut them off.
Come on, let's sing to the LORD! Let's shout to the rock who saves us!
Let's come into his presence with thanks and lift him up with songs. 🎶
The LORD is a great God, the great King above all gods.
He holds the deepest places on earth in his hand. The highest mountains are his too.
The sea is his because he made it. His hands shaped the dry land.
Come on, let's worship and bow down. Let's kneel before the LORD, our Maker,
because he's our God. We're the people in his pasture, the sheep in his care. If only you'd listen to his voice today!
Don't harden your hearts like at Meribah, like that day at Massah in the wilderness,
when your ancestors put me to the test even though they'd seen what I'd done.
For forty long years that generation grieved me. I said, “Their hearts keep going off course. They haven't learned my ways.”
So I swore in my anger, “They won't enter my rest.”
Sing the LORD a new song! Sing to the LORD, all the earth!
Sing to the LORD and bless his name! Tell how he saves, day after day. 🎶
Tell of his glory among the nations and the amazing things he's done among all peoples.
The LORD is great and deserves great praise! He's to be revered above all gods.
The gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Honor and majesty go before him. Strength and beauty fill his sanctuary.
Families of every nation, give the LORD his due. Give the LORD glory and strength.
Give the LORD the glory his name deserves. Bring an offering and come into his courts.
Worship the LORD in holy splendor. Tremble before him, all the earth.
Tell the nations, “The LORD reigns.” The world stands firm and can't be moved. He'll judge the peoples fairly.
Let the heavens be glad and the earth celebrate. Let the sea roar with everything in it! 🌊
Let the fields and everything in them celebrate. Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy
before the LORD, because he's coming to judge the earth. He'll judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his truth.
The LORD reigns! Let the earth celebrate! Let all the islands be glad!
Clouds and darkness surround him. Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
Fire goes ahead of him and burns up his enemies on every side.
His lightning lights up the world. The earth sees it and shakes. ⚡
The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of the whole earth.
The heavens tell of his righteousness. All the peoples have seen his glory.
Let everyone who serves carved images and brags about their idols be put to shame. All you gods, worship him!
Zion heard and was glad. The daughters of Judah celebrated because of your judgments, LORD.
You, LORD, are Most High over the whole earth. You're lifted far above all gods.
You who love the LORD, hate evil! He guards the lives of his faithful people and rescues them from the grip of the wicked.
Light is planted for people who do right, and joy for those with upright hearts.
Celebrate in the LORD, you who do what's right! Give thanks to his holy Name.
A psalm. Sing the LORD a new song! He's done amazing things. His right hand and his holy arm have won the victory.
The LORD has shown how he saves. He's put his righteousness on display for the nations to see.
He's remembered his faithful love and his faithfulness to the house of Israel. The farthest ends of the earth have seen our God save.
Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth! Burst into song and shout for joy! 🙌
Sing praise to the LORD with the harp. Let the harp and your voices make music together.
With trumpets and the blast of the ram's horn, shout for joy before the King, the LORD.
Let the sea roar with everything in it, and let the world and everyone in it join in.
Let the rivers clap their hands. Let the mountains sing for joy together
before the LORD, because he's coming to judge the earth. He'll judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with fairness.
The LORD reigns! Let the peoples tremble. He sits on his throne among the cherubim. Let the earth shake.
The LORD is great in Zion. He stands high above all the peoples.
Let them praise your great and awesome name. He is holy!
The mighty King loves justice. You set fairness in place. You do what's just and right in Jacob.
Lift up the LORD our God. Worship at his footstool. He is holy!
Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel was among those who called on his name. They called to the LORD, and he answered.
He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud. They kept the instructions and the rule he gave them.
LORD our God, you answered them. You forgave them and still held them to account for what they did.
Lift up the LORD our God. Worship at his holy hill, because the LORD our God is holy! 🙌
A psalm of thanksgiving. Shout for joy to the LORD, all you lands! 🙌
Serve the LORD with joy. Come into his presence singing.
Know that the LORD is God. He made us, and we belong to him. We're his people, the sheep of his pasture.
Walk through his gates with thanks and into his courts with praise. Thank him and bless his name.
The LORD is good. His faithful love lasts forever, and his faithfulness carries through every generation.
A psalm by David. I'll sing about faithful love and justice. LORD, I'll sing praise to you. 🎶
I'll pay attention to how I live and walk with integrity. When will you come to me? I'll live with an honest heart in my own home.
I won't put anything vile in front of my eyes. I hate what faithless people do, and I won't let their ways stick to me.
I'll keep a crooked heart far from me. I won't have anything to do with evil.
I'll silence anyone who secretly spreads lies about a neighbor. I won't put up with arrogant looks or a puffed-up heart.
I'll look to the faithful people of the land so they can live with me. Anyone who walks with integrity can serve me.
No one who practices deceit will live in my house. No one who tells lies will keep a place in my sight.
Morning after morning, I'll destroy the wicked in the land, cutting off everyone who does evil from the LORD's city.
A prayer for someone suffering, when it all gets too much and they pour out their troubles before the LORD. LORD, hear my prayer! Let my cry reach you.
Don't hide your face when I'm in distress. Lean in and hear me. When I call, answer me quick.
My days are burning away like smoke. My bones burn like a torch.
My heart is scorched and withered like grass. I even forget to eat.
I've groaned so much that I'm down to skin and bones.
I'm like a pelican in the wilderness, like an owl in a deserted place.
I lie awake, alone like a sparrow on the roof.
My enemies insult me all day. People raging at me use my name as a curse.
Ashes have been my bread. I've mixed tears into my drink,
because of your anger and wrath. You picked me up and threw me away.
My days stretch out like a long shadow. I've withered like grass.
But you, LORD, will remain forever. Your name will be remembered through every generation.
You'll rise and show mercy to Zion. It's time to have compassion on her. The appointed time has come.
Your servants love even her stones and feel for her when they see her dust.
The nations will revere the LORD's name, and every king on earth will stand in awe of your glory.
The LORD has rebuilt Zion and appeared in his glory.
He answered the prayer of those who had nothing. He didn't brush off their prayer.
Write this down for the next generation. People who haven't been created yet will praise the LORD,
because he looked down from his high sanctuary. From heaven, the LORD saw the earth,
to hear prisoners groan and free those sentenced to die,
so people can tell of the LORD's name in Zion and sing his praise in Jerusalem,
when peoples and kingdoms gather together to serve the LORD.
He drained my strength along the way. He cut my days short.
I said, “My God, don't take me away halfway through my life. Your years reach through every generation.
Long ago you laid the earth's foundation. The heavens are the work of your hands.
They'll perish, and you'll still be here. They'll all wear out like clothes. You'll change them like a coat, and they'll be changed.
But you're still the same. Your years will never end.
Your servants' children will live on, and their descendants will stand secure before you.”
By David. Praise the LORD, my soul! Everything in me, praise his holy name!
Praise the LORD, my soul. Don't forget all the good he's done for you.
He forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases.
He redeems your life from ruin and crowns you with faithful love and tender mercy.
He fills your life with good things so your youth is renewed like an eagle's.
The LORD does what's right and brings justice to everyone who's oppressed.
He showed Moses his ways and let the people of Israel see what he could do.
The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and overflowing with faithful love.
He won't keep accusing us or stay angry forever.
He hasn't treated us as our sins deserve or paid us back for the wrong we've done.
As high as the heavens are above the earth, that's how great his faithful love is for those who revere him.
As far as east is from west, that's how far he's taken our wrongs away from us.
Like a father who has compassion for his children, the LORD has compassion for those who revere him.
He knows how we're made. He remembers we're dust.
Our days are like grass. We flourish like wildflowers in a field.
The wind blows over a flower, and it's gone. Even the place where it grew forgets it.
The LORD's faithful love lasts from everlasting to everlasting for those who revere him. His righteousness reaches their grandchildren,
those who keep his covenant and remember to follow his instructions.
The LORD set his throne in the heavens. His kingdom rules over everything.
Praise the LORD, you mighty angels who carry out his word and obey his voice.
Praise the LORD, all his armies, all his servants who do what pleases him.
Praise the LORD, everything he's made, everywhere he rules. Praise the LORD, my soul! 🙌
Bless the LORD, my soul. LORD my God, you're so great! You're clothed in honor and majesty.
You wrap yourself in light like a robe and stretch out the heavens like a curtain.
You set the beams of your rooms in the waters. You make the clouds your chariot and walk on the wings of the wind.
You make winds your messengers and flames of fire your servants.
You laid the earth's foundations so it would stand firm forever.
You wrapped it in the deep like a cloak. The waters stood higher than the mountains.
At your rebuke the waters fled. At the sound of your thunder they rushed away.
The mountains rose and the valleys sank to the places you'd assigned them.
You set a boundary the waters can't cross, so they'll never cover the earth again.
You send springs into the valleys. They flow between the mountains.
They give every animal in the field a drink. Wild donkeys satisfy their thirst there.
Birds nest beside the streams and sing among the branches. 🎶
From your rooms you water the mountains. The earth is full of what your work produces.
You grow grass for livestock and plants for people to tend, so they can bring food out of the ground:
wine to bring joy to people's hearts, oil to make their faces shine, and bread to give them strength.
The LORD's trees have plenty of water, the cedars of Lebanon he planted,
where birds build their nests. The stork makes its home in the cypresses.
The high mountains are home to wild goats. The rocks give rock badgers a place to hide.
You made the moon to mark the seasons. The sun knows when to set.
You bring darkness and it becomes night, when all the forest animals come out to prowl.
Young lions roar for prey and look to God for food.
When the sun rises, they slip away and lie down in their dens.
People go out to work and keep at it until evening.
LORD, you've made so many things! You made every one of them with wisdom. The earth is full of what belongs to you.
Look at the sea, so big and wide, full of countless living things, creatures both tiny and huge.
Ships sail there, and Leviathan, whom you made to play in those waters, is there too. 🌊
All of them look to you to feed them at the right time.
You give them food and they gather it. You open your hand and they have their fill of good things.
When you hide your face, they're frightened. When you take away their breath, they die and go back to dust.
You send out your Spirit and they're created. You renew the face of the ground.
May the LORD's glory last forever. May the LORD take joy in what he's made.
He looks at the earth and it shakes. He touches the mountains and they smoke.
I'll sing to the LORD as long as I live. I'll sing praise to my God as long as I have breath.
May what I dwell on please him. I'll take joy in the LORD.
May sinners vanish from the earth, and may the wicked be gone. Bless the LORD, my soul. Praise the LORD!
Thank the LORD! Call on his name! Let all the peoples know what he’s done.
Sing to him! Sing his praises! Talk about every amazing thing he’s done.
Take pride in his holy name. Let everyone looking for the LORD rejoice from the heart.
Look to the LORD and his strength. Keep seeking his face, always.
Remember the amazing things he’s done, his wonders and the judgments he’s spoken,
you descendants of Abraham his servant, you children of Jacob, the ones he chose.
He’s the LORD our God. His judgments reach the whole earth.
He remembers his covenant forever, the word he gave for a thousand generations.
It’s the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac.
He confirmed it to Jacob as a lasting rule, to Israel as a covenant forever.
He said, “I’ll give you the land of Canaan. That’s your share, your inheritance.”
Back then they were only a handful, just a few people living there as foreigners.
They moved from one nation to the next, from one kingdom to another people.
He let no one mistreat them. He even called kings out for their sake:
“Don’t touch my anointed ones! Don’t harm my prophets!”
He called down famine on the land and cut off the food supply.
He sent someone ahead of them. Joseph was sold into slavery.
Shackles bruised his feet, and his neck was locked in iron,
until what Joseph said came true and the LORD’s word proved him right.
The king, the ruler of peoples, sent word to release him and let him go free.
He put Joseph over his household and gave him charge of everything he owned,
to discipline his princes as he saw fit and teach his elders wisdom.
Israel came to Egypt too. Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
The LORD made his people grow in number and made them stronger than their enemies.
He turned their enemies’ hearts to hate his people and plot against his servants.
He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, the one he chose.
They did miraculous signs among them and wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and the land went dark. They didn’t go against his words.
He turned their water into blood and killed their fish.
Frogs swarmed their land, getting even into their kings’ rooms.
He spoke, and swarms of flies and lice came all across their territory.
He sent hail instead of rain, with lightning flashing through their land.
He struck their vines and fig trees and shattered the trees across their country.
He spoke, and locusts and grasshoppers came in numbers nobody could count.
They ate every plant in the land and devoured what their soil had grown.
He struck down all the firstborn in their land, the first fruits of all their strength.
He led his people out with silver and gold, and not one in their tribes was too weak to go.
Egypt was glad to see them go because the Egyptians had come to fear them.
He stretched a cloud out to cover them and gave them fire to light the night.
They asked, and he brought quail. He gave them enough bread from the sky to satisfy them.
He opened the rock, and water gushed out. It ran like a river through the dry land.
He remembered his holy word and remembered Abraham, his servant.
He led his people out full of joy. The ones he chose came out singing.
He gave them the nations’ lands. They took possession of what other peoples had worked for,
so they could keep his statutes and follow his laws. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Thank the LORD because he’s good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Who could tell all the mighty things the LORD has done? Who could give him all the praise he deserves?
Blessed are the people who uphold justice and the person who does what’s right every time.
Remember me, LORD, when you show favor to your people. Come rescue me,
so I can see the people you chose thrive, celebrate with your nation, and take pride with the people who are your inheritance.
We’ve sinned right along with our ancestors. We’ve done wrong. We’ve acted wickedly.
Our ancestors didn’t get what your wonders in Egypt meant. They forgot your countless acts of faithful love and rebelled by the sea, right there at the Red Sea.
Still, he saved them for his name’s sake, to show how mighty his power is.
He told the Red Sea off, and it dried up. He led them through the depths like they were walking through a desert.
He saved them from the grip of the one who hated them and bought them back from the enemy’s hand.
The waters covered their enemies. Not one of them was left.
Then they believed what he said and sang his praises.
But they forgot what he’d done in no time. They didn’t wait for his advice.
They gave in to their cravings in the desert and put God to the test in the wasteland.
He gave them what they asked for but made their souls waste away.
In the camp they got jealous of Moses and of Aaron, the one set apart for the LORD.
The earth opened up and swallowed Dathan and buried Abiram’s whole group.
A fire broke out among them. The flames burned up the wicked.
At Horeb they made a calf and bowed to an image cast from metal.
They traded away their glory for a picture of a bull that eats grass.
They forgot God, the one who saved them and did great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham and awe-inspiring things by the Red Sea.
He said he’d wipe them out, but Moses, the one he chose, stood in the gap before him. He turned God’s anger away so God wouldn’t destroy them.
They looked down on that good land and didn’t believe what he said.
They grumbled in their tents and wouldn’t listen to the LORD’s voice.
So he swore he’d bring them down in the wilderness,
bring their descendants down among the nations, and scatter them through other lands.
They attached themselves to Baal Peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
What they did made him angry, and a plague broke out among them.
Then Phinehas stood up and carried out judgment, and the plague stopped.
That counted as righteousness for him through every generation to come.
They angered the LORD at the waters of Meribah too, and Moses suffered trouble on their account.
They rebelled against his spirit, and he spoke without thinking.
They didn’t destroy the peoples as the LORD told them to.
Instead they mixed with the nations and picked up their ways.
They served those nations’ idols, and the idols trapped them.
They even sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons.
They spilled innocent blood, the blood of their own sons and daughters, sacrificing them to the idols of Canaan. The blood polluted the land.
They made themselves unclean by what they did and sold themselves out through their actions.
So the LORD burned with anger at his people and was disgusted with his own inheritance.
He handed them over to the nations, and the people who hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies oppressed them and forced them to live under their control.
He rescued them over and over, but they kept making rebellious plans and were brought low by their own wrongdoing.
Even so, he saw how much they were hurting when he heard their cry.
He remembered his covenant with them and backed away from what he’d planned because his faithful love was so great.
He made the people who took them captive feel sorry for them.
Save us, LORD our God! Gather us from among the nations so we can thank your holy name and celebrate your praise!
Bless the LORD, the God of Israel, from forever to forever! Let all the people say, “Amen.” Praise the LORD!
Thank the LORD because he’s good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Let the people the LORD has rescued say so, the ones he bought back from the enemy’s grip,
and gathered from other lands, from east and west, north and south.
Some wandered along desert roads in the wilderness. They couldn’t find a city to call home.
Hungry and thirsty, they felt their life slipping away.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he rescued them from their distress.
He led them along a straight road so they could reach a city to live in.
Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and for the amazing things he does for people!
He satisfies the soul that’s longing and fills the hungry with good things.
Some sat in darkness, in the very shadow of death, bound by misery and iron.
They’d rebelled against God’s words and looked down on the Most High’s advice.
So he brought their spirits low with hard work. They fell down, and nobody was there to help.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
He brought them out of darkness and death’s shadow and snapped their chains.
Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and for the amazing things he does for people!
He broke through bronze gates and cut right through iron bars.
Some people were foolish and suffered because they disobeyed and did wrong.
They couldn’t stand any food and were near the gates of death.
Then they cry out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saves them from their distress.
He sends out his word and heals them. He rescues them from the grave.
Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and for the amazing things he does for people!
Let them bring sacrifices to thank him and sing about what he’s done.
Some go out to sea in ships and do business on great waters.
They see what the LORD does and the wonders he works in the deep.
He gives the command, and a storm wind rises and drives the waves up.
They shoot toward the sky, then plunge into the depths. In that danger, their courage melts away.
They lurch back and forth and stagger like drunk people. They’re at their wits’ end.
Then they cry out to the LORD in their trouble, and he brings them out of their distress.
He calms the storm, and its waves go still.
They’re glad the water is quiet, and he brings them to the harbor they wanted.
Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and for the amazing things he does for people!
Let them lift him up when the people gather and praise him where the elders sit.
He turns rivers into deserts and springs into thirsty ground.
He turns productive land into a salty wasteland because of the wrong the people there do.
He turns a desert into a pool and dry land into springs of water.
He settles hungry people there so they can build a city to live in.
They plant fields and vineyards and bring in good harvests.
He blesses them, and their numbers grow big. He doesn’t let their livestock shrink.
Then their numbers fall, and oppression, trouble, and sorrow bend them low.
He pours contempt on rulers and sends them wandering through a wasteland with no trails.
But he lifts needy people out of their suffering and makes their families grow like flocks.
Upright people see it and are glad, and all the wicked shut their mouths.
If you’re wise, pay attention to this. Think about the ways the LORD has shown his faithful love.
A song. A psalm by David. My heart is steady, God. I’m going to sing and make music with my whole soul.
Wake up, harp and lyre! I’ll wake up the dawn.
I’ll thank you, LORD, out among the nations. I’ll sing your praises among the peoples.
Your faithful love is bigger than the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches all the way to the skies.
Rise above the heavens, God! Let your glory cover the whole earth.
